utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stein.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Stein:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Zlotrg, if there's any question you don't understand, please let me know. I would like to have before the witness Exhibit Z245, please. Now, sir, until you came to The Hague, you never saw this document; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I gave it to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You gave it to the investigators from the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not there when this document was signed; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were physically present when this document was signed?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I was not present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not see the document being signed by the people who signed it; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is not true, sir?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was not present, so I could not have seen them sign the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And someone gave you the document to give to the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We acted in accordance with a telegram or, rather, in accordance with a document sent by the International Tribunal from The Hague. That is to say, the documents should be sent to The Hague Tribunal so that they could have insight into them. When this document arrived in my police station, I was in charge of collecting evidence from the ground, so all of that was according to the instructions of The Hague Tribunal, and I don't really have anything else to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you Document 245?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: From the Ministry of Defence of the municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who, specifically, gave you the document, what person?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The chief, Nijaz Sivro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where he got the document from?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had never seen this document before the chief gave it to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I acted according to the request of The Hague Tribunal. I collected documents that are relative to the Santic case, the Santic/Kupreskic case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question, sir. It's a very simple question. Until the chief of police gave you this document, you had never seen it before; "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not the chief of police. I got it from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're going round and round in circles, quite unnecessarily. Mr. Zlotrg, will you just answer the question? Had you seen this document before you sent it here? Had you seen it at any time?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Exactly. Now, can we move on, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Certainly, Sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also true that you had never seen the individuals who signed this document sign other documents; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that I saw Islam or -- I don't know, other members of the Muslim people. I saw Nenad Santic when he was signing a bill, because he worked at the gasoline station in Vitez. But whether the signature is authentic or not, there are experts who can ascertain that. I'm not an expert. I can't say that this is his signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. That's exactly the point I wanted to make. Now, I would like to turn our attention to another area, and that is crimes perpetrated against Croats during the same period of time that you testified to, and I will be very brief. You're aware, sir, on January 10, 1993, there was a grenade thrown from the Mahala area of Stari Vitez that killed -- I'm sorry, June, 1993, June 10 -- that killed 10 Croat children; you're aware of that, aren't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was a war, and I don't know. As far as shelling is concerned, I don't know. I wasn't in the area that was under HVO control, I was in Zenica at the time. As far as I can remember, I was exchanged on the 16th of May, 1993, and I spent that entire period in Zenica until the cease-fire was signed, that is to say, sometime around May 1994, when it was possible to return to Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were at your liberty on June 10, 1993, were you not?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were working as a policeman in Zenica at the time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I was a member of the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you doing for the army in June of 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was working in security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of security; police-type security?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, this is the army establishment. Well, security within the members of the army on the territory that is under our control, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you join the army, sir?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: A few days after the exchange. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would have been in May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were from the Stari Vitez area, were you not? That's where you lived?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I lived in town. Had I been in Stari Vitez, I wouldn't have been arrested. I lived in the street of Marsala Tita A1A4, building A1A4. That is to say, that is the part that was under HVO control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Were you aware, from the Mahala region, of a sniper team in 1993, after your release from incarceration, that killed five people and wounded 26?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know how many people were killed, but there was a sniper team in the HVO too. So it's an army, and it depends on how strong an army is. Some armies have more snipers. As far as I know, in Vitez there was one sniper, and on the side of the HVO, there were quite a few. And now you have to look at the proportion, how many people one side killed and how many people the other side killed. But there was a war that was going on, and when we were allies, even then we were hurt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is, yes, you were aware of snipers --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then let's get a clear "Yes" or "No." Were you aware, sir, "Yes" or "No," of whether there was a sniper team in the town of Stari Vitez, in the Mahala section, that killed five people and wounded 26?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that, because I was not in Stari Vitez. We did not have any communications, and whatever communications existed, it was done through coding, so you couldn't really go into such detail. And then you would have to have Mr. Sefkija Djidic, who was chief of staff, and he knew who was under his command. I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take your prior answer to mean that you were aware, however, that snipers and sniper teams were used by both Croats and Muslims during the course of this war.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I assume so, but I don't know whether there were snipers in Vitez or not, because I wasn't in Vitez at the time, so I really don't know. And I wasn't a member of the army until the second half of May, that is to say, when I was exchanged. That is when I joined the army ranks. But again, I had nothing to do with the units. I was involved in operations that had to do with security, and I didn't really have anything to do with sniper teams and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask one final question about these snipers. We can agree, can we not, sir, that snipers or sniper teams find a high place in which to shoot down from onto their victims; can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I imagine that that is sniper strategy. I was never on a sniper team, so I really don't know. I know about that only from the newspapers and from the movies. And if that can help you by way of an answer, all right, but I really don't know. I'm not a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know the name Mirsad Tatarevic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He's a colleague of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was one of the sniper teams that I was just talking about, wasn't he? He was a sniper?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, he had an automatic rifle issued to him. We called these rifles "Ciganka." It's a kind of Kalashnikov. The police did not have any snipers. As far as I know, he was a policeman in Stari Vitez, together with me, and he stayed there with his personal weapons. He had a pistol and a rifle, and I know that he got out of the war with that rifle. But what happened in Stari Vitez, that I cannot tell you because that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whether or not he took that automatic rifle and climbed to a high place and shot Croats, you don't know; is that what you're telling me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has said he doesn't know what the man did with the rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Very good, Sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Sefkija Djidic. You know who he is; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was commander of the staff of the Territorial Defence, and when the conflict broke out, he held that position. The few Muslims that had remained in Stari Vitez managed to defend themselves from the aggression of the HVO. That is what I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between April 16, 1993, and February 25, 1994, the army of BH under his command took over the Mahala section of Stari Vitez; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, they did not take anything, they defended themselves in the area of Stari Vitez so that nothing would happen to them. Had no one offered resistance in Stari Vitez, then there would have been a repetition of Ahmici. That is to say that they defended themselves. They did not take anything. All the Croats --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Zlotrg, I must ask you to answer questions briefly, if you would. We'll get this over more quickly. If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under his command, 37 civilians were detained in Stari Vitez, those civilians being all Croats. You're aware of that, aren't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. They were not detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were allowed to be at their liberty; is that what you're telling the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were free.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like you to be shown, please, Document 332,2, and this is my final area of questioning. Sir, when Mr. Nice introduced this document, Report of Witness Interview, he called it a judicial statement setting out facts. This, in fact, was a record of your appearance in the High Court in Zenica; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to what I can see here, I guess it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the judge before whom you appeared was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the court clerk was a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the proceedings were criminal proceedings against the accused Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't have any jurisdiction over the High Court in Zenica. That is what the team was, and I made a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to burden the record, but the first paragraph speaks for itself, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The facts that you presented are set out in this document. I would like to turn to those facts. Specifically, the English version would be on page 2 and the Croatian version would similarly be on the first full page. You told that court, and I'll read the quote that I'd like you to focus on, it's about the fourth full paragraph. The facts you presented to the court were contained at the fifth paragraph, the next to last paragraph on page 2, Your Honours, and I'm quoting: "In order to avoid analysing all the conditions, circumstances, and contentions of the HZ-HB as a witness, I will focus on the specific actions of extremists in the area of our municipality, as well as on the consequences of their actions, because it is these consequences that define each and every Croat's participating in the realisation of said plan. I can say that they were all in on this plan, soldiers, policemen, even civilians, young and old. Even their women played a part. They were all engaged in implementing their plan of genocide by committing the most possible crimes against the Muslims, mostly civilian, population." Those are the facts that you presented to the court; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you believe those facts today, as you now testify, do you not?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. How would you comment on this, if the women did not allow Red Cross teams to come in and evacuate a 15-day-old baby? Because the pregnancy did not come to term, and this baby could have survived only in an incubator. They tried to get into Stari Vitez at five different points, at least that's what they told us via the communications we had, the Red Cross team; however, they didn't manage to get the baby out. I was the officer on duty at the time, and I was in contact with them, and the baby died. It was the baby of Adnan Adilovic. I found out later about that. If that is not an indicator that women and others participated, I don't know what else we should be looking for, not to speak of stopping humanitarian convoys going to Kruscica, et cetera, et cetera, all kinds of blockades. They do this until the present day. Again, they are putting women and children to stop the Muslim people from coming to the villages where their politicians say that they can freely come back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Croats are all involved, and they are all guilty; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No, I never said all of them, but they did use women and children and old men. That was the essence of the statement I made to Mr. Adilovic. Re-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the same page, the previous paragraph, maybe the Tribunal has already read it, but if you look at the previous paragraph to the one that was quoted to you, there is another paragraph setting out, in a summary view, your view of the history of what had happened. It begins, "Thus, I learned that the Croats, by their political party, had drawn up a project." Did you set out or did the person making the statement set out there a summary of your overall view, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. But this is what I got as a member of the army because we, in the security section, also received information, and wherever I was sure, I gave the date, place, et cetera, and put it all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that when Mr. Stein speaks of facts, just remind the Tribunal of the format of this document, the hard identified facts by date and sometimes even by time are set out on later pages; is that correct? Have a look at the statement.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, on the later pages, you can see that, even the possible perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since we may not, all of us or any of us, be familiar with the format for taking a statement like this -- you certainly did it once, you may have done it more than once, I don't know -- can you tell the Tribunal how this form of statement came to be prepared? Was it done with a preparatory document? Was it done with question and answer? Was it done by dictation? How? Just explain it for us, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I came before the court to make a statement about the events that, unfortunately, I took part in as well. When I gave the statement, I had access to all the documents of the Public Security Station, all the remaining documents, that is, all that were not destroyed during war operations. At that time, I was going through all these documents, so the record I gave to the judge is far more extensive than the reminder I have, the notes we mentioned. I worked with the judge for two days. During the first day, we talked in general terms about what I could remember and what I knew. The next day, I came with documents, and whatever had a specific date, I read that document. I also gave it to the prosecutor so they could make photocopies for themselves. The judge put questions in respect of that that he was particularly interested in, and as far as other matters were concerned, they were simply recorded in this record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is how I gave the statement, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were questions about whether the judge and, I think, the prosecutor were each Muslims. Did that, in any way, affect whether you were telling the truth or not?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's deal with documents a little more comprehensively because you've been asked many questions about them. First of all, you had the records of complaints made by members of the public which have been exhibited in this Court.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then made the statement we've just been looking at in October of 1994 to the judge, and at that time, you had more documents available to you.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that when you were making entries or when entries were made in this statement to the judge and you signed it, contemporaneous documents assisted your memory?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, because, more or less, I processed every report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then made the later statement -- you made the notes in 1996, all of which have been served on the Defence, for the purposes of talking to the Office of the Prosecutor here; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you made those notes, did you have access to your statement to the judge in 1994 or not?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've been shown by the Defence several documents. I'd like you, please, to have them all before them again, and we can deal with them quite, I hope, comprehensively.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's D4/2, and he need only have them in the original form, and I think he already probably has D4/2 in front of him. D5/2, D6/2, which we still, I don't think, have a translation. I don't know if one is being provided. D6/2, no translation. D9/2, D10/2, D11/2, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you would like to take these documents in front of you and leave them in the pile in which they come to you and probably clear everything else away from the table, you will find it more easier, I think. The first question I want you to answer in relation to each of these documents is whether you have seen any of them before. The second in relation to each of these documents is whether even if you haven't seen them before in their original form, they are in a general form or format that you recognise. Do you understand the two questions? Do you understand the two questions, Mr. Zlotrg?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen the document before? If not, is it, nevertheless, in a format that you recognise? So starting with D4/2, have you seen that before you came to court last week? That's the report of --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the form, the format of it something that you would recognise as being genuine and appropriate?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first thing that is missing on this document is the number of the document. There is only a date, but it has not been filed. There is nothing about it being processed, and correspondence with one's superiors cannot be done that way. At least Budimir taught us when he worked with us that you had to give every document a number, because a document such as this one could have been written at any time because there's no where the number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there with that document. Put that one temporarily on one side. D5/2, do you have that?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's the general analysis. Perhaps the usher could help him just to make sure that the markings on the top are reflected by the documents he's looking at. D5/2 is the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If they were all handed in the correct order, they should be in the correct order. Usher, will you stay there, please, because you will be able to help him some more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: D5/2, is that a document you've ever seen before?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Here in the courtroom for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The form of the document or the type of document, is it something that you recognise or not?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a general analysis. It does not go into any explanation, but when you do an analysis, then there is also a proposal of measures to overcome the situation for which it was done, and there's nothing of that sort here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But does it fit with the type of document being prepared at the time or not or can't you say?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: All I can say is how the army worked. One thing is certain, they did not do it in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Document D6/2, the one which has no translation, a single sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: They were all handed in the right order. That's the one, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid there was an error. The first document which my colleague, Mr. Nice, mentioned, 4/2, this is a document which does have -- the court document, the on-site investigation, this one does have the date and number and everything. Obviously, there was some confusion, because the witness said, looking at the document, "There is no date, no number," et cetera. So obviously there was some confusion. I'm not objecting. I'm just pointing out that there is some confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'll deal with it. It may be a photocopying problem. I'll deal with it as soon as I come back to it, which I will very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't have a copy of that, I don't know why, but at some time I'd like a copy of D4/2, please. No need to bother with it at the moment. Have you got one? Likewise, for Judge Bennouna. Mr. Nice, can we deal with this fairly rapidly?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm trying to deal with it rapidly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It's leading to confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. The points have got to be dealt with. I shall deal with it quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: D6/2, just very briefly, that document, have you ever seen it before coming to court?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now please take D9/2 dated the 21st of January, 1993? We do have a translation. Had you ever seen that document before coming to court?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: D10/2, which we do have a translation of, had you ever seen that document before coming to court?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we leave that document, one paragraph in it, indeed, paragraph 1, speaks of Muslims reporting to the -- well, it appears the Stefan Tomasevic Brigade, requesting to join that unit. One way or another, do you know if that happened? Did Muslims apply to join that brigade at about this time, January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, D11/2, had you ever seen that document before you came to court?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One question about this. We have a translation. It said that at five minutes past midnight, the apartment of Zoran Krizanovic was hit by a hand-held rocket launcher. Did you know something about that as an event?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who fired the launcher?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The rocket was launched from under the balcony of the family of Dragan Drmic, and that is the same building where my brother and sister-in-law lived, those who were killed by members of the Croatian Defence Council. The target was not the apartment but the coffee shop Italia owned by Ibrahim Topcic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a Muslim or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shall we now go back, please, to D4/2, and for this purpose, I think the Court should have the document before it. I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: All right. Maybe, in light of the observations, all the other documents may now be taken away to make life easier for the witness and the usher, and just leave, please, the witness with D4/2, which is the on-site investigation report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have that report before you?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I have a look at it, please, Usher, just to make sure that it's not a photocopying error or shortcoming that gives rise to Mr. Kovacic's point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the top right-hand corner, there is a stamped box with the date "19/6/92" on it. Had you taken that box into account when you said that there was no number on the document?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no. No, I did not look at this document when I mentioned the number. It was when I spoke about the analysis, and that is when I said that it was missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then I am grateful to Mr. Kovacic. This document does have a number on it, does it?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Both the court file and also the number which was put in by the clerk at the Public Security Station which was filed -- it was on the 19th of June of '92, and then it was filed when this document reached the station. That is the rule when it comes to correspondence between institutions or units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you accepting, I suppose you are, that this is a report properly prepared and filed?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As to its content, just help the Tribunal with a few details, now that we've got it in translation. Does the report contain anywhere an explanation of what eyewitnesses had seen of the killing? If so, point to the paragraph; if not, say so.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The document only says that about witnesses who were found but not the statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any explanation of why the man Vukadinovic was being apparently sought or was an object of inquiry?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Something is wrong with the witness's microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It says that Vukadinovic was in flight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says that he was in flight, but it doesn't say what the evidence was to show that he might have been guilty, does it?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were any efforts made to track down and arrest the man Vukadinovic?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, nothing was done, as far as I know, because after a while he was moving about the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long after?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly, but it was before the conflict. That I know. I believe it was a few months later that he was seen, perhaps a month or two. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any autopsy reports or fingerprint reports obtained, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He was working for Zenica, and I brought him from Zenica up there. And there was Mr. Franjo present, and myself as the criminal technician. But as I was a junior technician, I was doing other things, and Franjo was there. And the record had to be made of the autopsy done by Dr. Tucic, who did the post-mortem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last question on this document, now that the Tribunal has it, on page 1, the second-to-last paragraph, and it will be at a similar place on the original, the paragraph reads: "The duty officer in the Vitez SJB also informed the duty judge over the telephone that for security reasons, it was not possible to go to the scene of the incident immediately and that it would only be possible to carry out the investigation in the morning." Can you help us, please, with what, if any, detail of the security reasons was given to justify the delay or to explain the delay?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, the on-site investigation could have been conducted that same night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is was there any detail given of the reasons?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, we were not told anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think I omitted to deal with the ethnic origin of the victim, Trako. With leave, may I just establish that through the witness now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Trako, what ethnic group was he?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked questions about rumours concerning Cerkez in this matter, and I want you to confine your answer to the next two questions exactly to what I ask you. When did you first learn of the rumours, approximately, in relation to the death?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, a few days later, after he was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next question is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. A couple of days ago, we were discussing the category of rumours. It is even more than hearsay, as I understood. And again it is the same question, "When you heard the rumours about it."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I mean I think there was some cross-examination on that rumour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Absolutely. May I make the position quite clear? I was cut short at an early stage in my examination-in-chief when I was dealing with the state of rumours, but I wasn't going to elicit -- if anybody had asked me, I wasn't going to elicit the person to whom the rumours were connected at that stage, in any event. But I wanted simply to establish, in case later evidence of value may be able to assist, when and by what route rumours were circulating. And then that fact will fit in or, alternatively, not fit in and guide the Chamber. And so my next question, and the only other question I desire on this topic, is from whom did rumours come to this person, because that may or may not fit in with better evidence. But absent better evidence, this will remain rumour and I shan't rely on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. The re-examination is allowed to include a question of fact, which is, "Where did you hear something?" That refers to the fact that something was said, without going into any detail of what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you, Sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next question, please -- and again just answer the question with a name or similar. Don't expand on the answer. From whom, if you can now remember, from whom did you hear the rumour?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: A number of people; not one, several people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name any of them?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I can't, really. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. That's all I want to know. You were asked about this being in or not in certain statements. Did you include this in your statement to the judge in 1994, the fact of the rumours?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you also tell the OTP about it in one of your many statements?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The position of Cerkez as commander, you were asked about. What period do you say he was commander in Vitez? If you can be precise or approximate, but if you can't even be approximate, say so.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first half of '92 is when he was appointed, but I don't know when, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had been asked about the Herzegovinian members or Herzegovinians in the area as members of the HVO. Can you tell us what period you were aware of their presence there as a group or as an identity?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were present, I think, as of the latter half of '92 and participated actively in conflicts in '93. I don't remember exactly when, and it wasn't a group, it was an organised unit which took shifts. And for all the incidents, our local Croats blamed them for all these incidents, and yet they did nothing to take them back from wherever they had come from, because we had no conflict with the Croatian Defence Council units. So I really saw no reason why they should be quartered with us here and why not on the line against the Serbs in Herzegovina. So it meant that they were here with a purpose in mind, to learn the lie of the ground and then perform some jobs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To help you come to the end of your evidence, I only have a few more questions to ask of you. Confine your answers to the questions I ask. You referred to where they were quartered. Where were they quartered? Was it separate from or along with other groups?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Separately. They were accommodated in the elementary school in Dubravica. And to the best of my knowledge, they were alone there, they were by themselves there. But we were not allowed access there. I know that in one instance, they controlled me. They ordered me out of their vehicle, even though we had tried to persuade them that it had been agreed with the civilian police of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. It took them a long time to let us through, even though we showed them our police IDs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Several terms, just two or three, I think, that have been used. The word "interned" has been used, the word "detained," possibly the word "imprisoned," and the word "camp" has been used. Can you distinguish between "internment," "detention," and "imprisonment," or are these words to you the same?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say "Yes," meaning that the words are the same?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The word "camp" --

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- has been used through the services of the interpreters. What do you mean by "camp"?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a place where they kept us without any living conditions. In the reception centre in Zenica, they had electric power, they had three meals a day. Each of them had his bunkbed, and they also had walks every day. And I was put up -- packed like a sardine. I could not turn. And we had a quarter of a loaf of bread and a tin for the whole day. There was nothing else, no --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me this: When you were interned, imprisoned, or detained in a camp, were you there voluntarily or not? What, so far as you were concerned, was your position?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Without my consent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was suggested to you by Mr. Stein, I think, that there was no ill treatment in either the camps or in Kaonik when you were there. Did you personally see any ill treatment?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Physically, they did not beat us, but they would enter drunk, with weapons; that is, with a rifle or a pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see any physical ill treatment. Did you hear anything consistent with physical ill treatment, yourself, while you were there?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard blows, and I heard screams, and begging them not to beat them. That was what I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, finally, did you hear of any ill treatment from others while you were there?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: While we were there, nobody talked, because we had no contact with other prisoners. On one occasion, I think they made a mistake, and Samija from Vitez, he was quite a well-off man, had stayed with us for lunch for about 10 or 15 minutes until they saw -- realised they had made a mistake and removed him. But then he did not say anything. He only said he was having it very hard. We were not allowed to talk, or else anything might have happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next thing, you were asked questions about trench digging, and you spoke of dead bodies being brought back from trench digging --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One moment. There's an objection. Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting, but I think there was an error in the transcript. It is quite an important place, and Mr. Nice was asking deliberately about two places together. He was -- the question was related to both internment places, cinema and Kaonik, and the witness said that he had heard about beatings in Kaonik, and that is not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That, in fact, was his original evidence, as I remember it. He spoke about Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, but here, suddenly there is no "Kaonik."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Nice --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It can be corrected. I'm quite happy about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you clear that up?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The sounds of beatings, were they in one place or were they in both places? Was it just Kaonik or was it Kaonik and the other places?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Only Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Only when we were about to be exchanged in Vitez, Mr. Suad Salkic from a member of the HVO was beaten by a member of HVO on the 14th of May, that is, when we were brought back from Kaonik. That was the only case of ill treatment that I saw in Vitez, because he took Mr. Salkic out into the passage through one door, and at the other door he had a stick. He had a pole of about a metre, a metre and a half, and some 10 centimetres diameter. He forced him back into the room, and he hid amongst us, because otherwise he would have killed him. He wasn't looking where he was hitting him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Trench digging and bodies coming back from trench digging, is this something you ever saw, yourself, something you heard of, and if you only heard of it, from whom?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not see this myself, but there was information going around, and we also received information when someone was wounded or killed. And later, as we talked to family members, this was confirmed. Adis Tuco was killed while digging trenches. And I cannot recall all the other names, but their parents or their brothers or sisters later confirmed to us that these persons, these young men, did not return from trench digging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've been asked about the command function, which you say did not exist. While you were there, was there any evidence of a distinction between military and political control and command?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sometime in '92, I think it was mid-1992, the HDZ was separated from the army. However, approximately when they first drove us out at the station, then the Croatian Defence Council started to operate. The very name, the Croatian Defence Council, means that everything is mobilised, that there is a state of war, conditionally speaking, and that it is politics that should command the military. I don't know what it was like in their case, but I'm saying what it was like in our case. The war presidency had jurisdiction over the Vitez Brigade, so I imagine that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- I imagine that the president of the municipality had certain powers over the Vitez Brigade of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll cut you off. You were using the word "imagine." I wanted to know if you saw any evidence of a separation between political and military control, and if you don't have any such evidence, we'll move on to the next question. And there are only about three to go. It was suggested by Mr. Stein, at one stage, that in preparing your statement, you had selectively picked from the raw material available to you in making your chronology of events and statements. But the word "selectively" wasn't qualified. Had you, in fact, selected material that was related to Muslims being victims from the material at the police station or had you set out all the events over the relevant period of time in making your notes and statements?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: First, I should answer the first question. When the Croatian Defence Council was proclaimed, then all the politicians started wearing camouflage uniforms with insignia of the Croatian Defence Council, and that's the way they walked around Vitez. And that is why my assumption is based on that. That is to say, that they had powers over the Vitez Brigade of the HVO. I presented all the material that was accessible to me. I would have done the same thing had I had recorded somewhere that a Croat had lodged a complaint. I can't remember the name of a Croat, but he had registered a vehicle with us, and then the Croats in Jablanica took off his license plates because he had license plates saying "Bosnia-Herzegovina." But I do not recall the date, and I think his name is Vladimir, Vlado, something like that, so I couldn't mention him here. Also, I know that Croats who were not loyal were taken to Mount Kruscica and were mistreated there, but they took those people who were not members of the HDZ. That is to say those who were members of the SDP. Overnight, they stopped being members --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll cut you short. I think you've given the answer. You've included all the material. And then this about the Ahmici agreement, you've made reference to somebody called Sivro Nijaz, from whom you obtained the statement. And the Court will possibly recall that when I touched on this in evidence in chief, I identified this statement to the Office of the Prosecutor where all this was out. It's the 22nd of October, 1992, to guide my friends if they want to find it. But who was Sivro Nijaz? He's been referred to as a chef. Who was he, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he was not a chef. He's chief of --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I meant "chief." Sorry, Mr. Zlotrg. My mistake for picking up one word in the original. What was he?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was chief of the Secretariat of National Defence in Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the communications that had led to him handing the document to you had gone by what route; do you know? Do you know to whom the ICTY, the Office of the Prosecutor, had first communicated in order to bring about Sivro Nijaz from the Ministry of Defence handing the document to you?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received the original from Nijaz Sivro, and I had it photocopied, and I gave it to the OTP. But the gentleman could not give me the original for keeps because he kept it in the archives. And then I told the OTP that Nijaz Sivro sent the document to the Cantonal Secretariat of National Defence and that they should talk to the cantonal ministry in Travnik. And I don't know what happened then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the original request had gone from the ICTY to the Federal Ministry of Interior Affairs?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know, but when I attended the trial of Vladimir Santic, the document had reached The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, finally, you've been asked about Stari Vitez, and the words "taken over" were used. So far as you were aware, were Croats detained against their will in the course of what you have described as a defensive action?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. As a matter of fact, one Croat didn't want to leave when they asked for him to go to the new town of Vitez. He stayed throughout, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You told us about him already. Thank you. Thank you very much. That concludes all I ask in re-examination. There's a transcript error at page 34, line 18, where, in dealing with Croats not loyal, as the Court will immediately recollect, the transcript, by oversight, says "loyal" as opposed to "not loyal," so may it be corrected to reflect what he said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The question I want to ask is not specifically related to the re-examination. It does relate to the Document D9/2, and I would be grateful if the witness could be given that document, D9/2. Do you have it? Do you have D9/2?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not the complete document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Could you give him the complete document? Do you have the complete document now?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The document is dated the 25th of January, 1993, and it's a report on the activities of groups and individuals acting without the knowledge of the HVO command. It then goes on to list a number of activities which are apparently criminal activities, crimes that were committed. I wanted to ask you whether, in the period covered by your testimony, whether you're able to distinguish between activities that were criminal and activities that were politically motivated, in the sense that they were ethnically inspired. Were you able to make that distinction?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the same document, there are about six references to crimes committed by different persons. If we're to take, for example, the first one, which is "aggravated robbery," are you able to say whether that was committed wholly by the persons whose names are mentioned there or whether it was committed by them in conjunction with soldiers?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were members of the Croatian Defence Council. But at the end where Mr. Budimir says that they give the uniform a bad name, then one does assume that all of them are members of the Croatian Defence Council. Had they locked up these dozen or so immediately and sanctioned this, then nothing would have happened, but they do not say here in this report that all the victims were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: So this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- both political and criminal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you say, in the period covered by your testimony, what was the extent of criminal activities?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could you please somehow explain this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me go a little further. Were criminal activities at a higher rate than they would be normally in the period covered by your testimony?

utterances.speaker: EDIB ZLOTRG (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, there was much, much more criminal activity. In normal times, we did not know of robbery. It was only pilfering that happened and perhaps disturbances of law and order, but aggravated robbery, armed robbery, things like that, these grave crimes never occurred before in our parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Zlotrg, thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give your evidence. You are now released. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, are you in a position to call the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to ask for a couple of minutes in any event, but before Mr. Scott takes the next witness in chief, I would like a couple of minutes myself before he does that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It's coming up to the time that we would adjourn. Shall we say 4.00? Who is the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He's a witness in respect of whom an application for closed session will probably be made, and it can't be in open session. Which document would presently prove to be the most useful guide? Because I can't obviously give the name here until the question of the -- are you relying on the summaries? The last edition of the summaries might be a way of guiding you to it or I can simply tell Ms. Featherstone when you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. That might be the quicker way to do it. Has an application in writing been made?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, it has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We probably have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Number 224 in the latest revised edition, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If he's the subject of the latest application, I think we will be able to find it quite quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The application of the 13th of April. I'm grateful to Ms. Verhaag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: What is the number in your list of witnesses, the revised list?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In the list of witnesses, then it's number 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: Number 11? In which category of your --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think Your Honour is referring to a different -- I'm sorry. Your Honours are referring to a different document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I've got it. It's this one, the 13th of April. We've got that. We will adjourn now until 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before we turn to the next witness, the interpreters have very kindly drawn to my attention the fact that at one place in the re-examination of the last witness, the format of my question led to an answer that is misleading. It can be found on page 1894, line 15, where I was asking about the terms "imprisonment," "detention," and "internment," whether they were the same to him or different. By unwisely incorporating the next question that I had in mind about the use of the word "camp," where the witness said "Yes," the word, according to the interpreter, should have been "No," i.e., he was not accepting that the imprisonment, internment, and detention were the same concept to him. I know it had been raised in the course of cross-examination, and I don't know whether anything will be built on it. At the end, he told us that his detention was against his will. I don't apply for him to be brought back, but before he leaves The Hague, I thought I'd at least explain the position to the Court in case the Court thinks anything of significance may turn on it, so that he could come back and explain the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I thought he meant precisely the same. I thought he said "Yes," meaning they were the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The answer should, according to the interpreters, have been, "No, they were different."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I can't myself think that anything turns on it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In which case, Ms. Verhaag can go and tell him that he may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next witness is one in respect of whom an application will be made by Mr. Scott. I have, as I undertook to do, checked with every witness the position, mindful of the desire of everyone here that, as much as possible, it should be in open court. But I must ask the Court, please, to go into closed session to hear the application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: 5.26 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of May, 1999, at 2.30 p.m.
